name: Decoy and receiver
engine: Never give it to Oyarzabal: his marker follows him, so every cut-back goes to Olmo, who has not touched the ball yet.
about: Found by the simulations, not designed: the Decoy (wave E) and Nominated receiver (wave A) were worth +0.18 goals a match more together than apart, the biggest pair measured across all waves. At the start of each attack a centre-back of theirs goes wherever Oyarzabal goes: a pass to him or a move by him is -2, and a move by anyone else against one of their defenders is +1, until Oyarzabal touches the ball. Every cut-back and low cross goes to Olmo instead of Oyarzabal, so Oyarzabal never touches it and the +1 lasts. If Olmo has not had the ball earlier in the attack, a clean win on his shot needs 3, not 4 (Fresh feet); when he shoots unmarked it needs only 2 (Cool head). Two clean wins in a row give the attack one more decision (Rhythm), and the +1 makes clean wins likelier.
decisions: Keep the ball away from Oyarzabal: every pass to him ends the +1 for the rest of the attack.
Keep Olmo out of the build-up: his shot is best when the cut-back is his first touch.
Go for clean wins early: two in a row buy one more decision.
